FDA labeling gives a starting dose of 300 mg three times daily and a recommended maintenance range of 300 to 600 mg three times daily; clinical study text reports a statistically significant responder-rate difference at 900 mg/day.

fact_checks.rationale: The current value is directionally supported, but the proposed wording is closer to the FDA label and avoids implying that all higher dosing is merely extra-label practice.

fact_checks.rationale: FDA labeling supports 300 to 600 mg three times daily for patients 12 years and older and notes higher administered doses.

rct_link_checks.label: Yamauchi2006
rct_link_checks.rationale: PubMed record supports gabapentin, randomized assignment, double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group design, refractory partial seizures, and 1200/1800 mg/day adjunctive therapy.

rct_link_checks.label: Zhu2005
rct_link_checks.rationale: PubMed abstract supports gabapentin vs placebo in a double-blind multicenter refractory epilepsy trial. Outcome percentages for RR50/MPC/SF are not extractable from the abstract.

rct_link_checks.label: Appleton1999
rct_link_checks.rationale: PubMed abstract supports a 12-week multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized pediatric refractory partial-seizure trial of gabapentin add-on therapy.

rct_link_checks.label: Leach1997
rct_link_checks.rationale: Record supports a double-blind, dose-ranging, placebo-controlled crossover study of adjunctive gabapentin in refractory epilepsy, but seizure-frequency RR50/MPC/SF outcomes are not extractable from the abstract.

rct_link_checks.label: Trudeau1996
rct_link_checks.rationale: The publication reports two double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter gabapentin studies in childhood absence epilepsy. It verifies drug/design/placebo but does not support focal-seizure efficacy.

rct_link_checks.label: Dimond1996
rct_link_checks.proposed_action: flag for user review before retaining as a phase II/III RCT link
rct_link_checks.rationale: The abstract describes a review/secondary analysis of global improvement data from five double-blind clinical trials, not an independent primary phase II/III seizure-efficacy RCT report. It should not be used for RR50/MPC/SF outcomes.

rct_link_checks.label: BenMenachem1995
rct_link_checks.rationale: PubMed supports gabapentin in a placebo-controlled double-blind study in intractable complex partial seizures, with RCT publication type. The abstract focuses on CSF parameters and does not provide extractable RR50/MPC/SF outcomes.

rct_link_checks.label: Anhut1994
rct_link_checks.rationale: Publication is a multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled add-on gabapentin study in refractory partial seizures and supports the RR50 differential used in the row.

rct_link_checks.label: PMID1993
rct_link_checks.rationale: PubMed/Neurology abstract supports a 12-week multicenter, placebo-controlled, parallel-group gabapentin add-on trial in refractory partial epilepsy. The abstract provides responder-rate range but not a maximum-dose-specific differential without supplemental sources.

rct_link_checks.label: Sivenius1991
rct_link_checks.rationale: PubMed supports a double-blind, placebo-controlled add-on gabapentin study in partial and secondarily generalized seizures. The abstract reports a 57% decrease for the 1200 mg arm but not enough placebo-arm percentage detail for the row's plotted differential outcomes.

rct_link_checks.label: PMID1990
rct_link_checks.rationale: The deterministic warning is not upheld. The abstract explicitly states multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group gabapentin add-on therapy in drug-resistant partial epilepsy, and reports the RR50 and MPC values used in the row.

summary: Core gabapentin pharmacology, dosing, formulation, adverse-event, focal-seizure indication, year-approval, and most RCT-link facts are supported by FDA/NCBI/PubMed sources. Updates are needed for the boxed-warning source, Horizant trade-name handling, enzyme-effect filter, trusted evidence source names, and seizure-freedom extraction from Appleton1999. PMID 1971862 is a valid gabapentin placebo-controlled RCT despite its nonspecific title.
